findings.reason: without saying that the refused launch is one the launch path starts and then collects as a failure, the node can write its control against a pre-launch refusal, watch it pass at base, and either weaken the test or block, which is the wrong path this section exists to prevent.
findings.text: §17's gate says the first case must fail at base "with the backend field moved", but the only base behaviour that moves the pointer while reporting a refused launch is a launch that starts and is then collected as failed: every pre-launch refusal raises before the mutation, so a test fixture that refuses the launch where a test author would naturally put it (a launcher that raises) passes on the unfixed code and the negative control proves nothing

response_events.note: the first case is now the observed shape: a lane change whose launch is accepted and whose worker never starts, which is what moved the pointer on the base; a refusal raised before launch is a separate case that must pass on both

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the incident run id resolves to a live pointer, §17/§23/§24 resolve as sections, and the test paths are new deliverables rather than citations.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §17 at :165 treats "a lane change whose launch is refused" as a case that fails at the base revision with the backend field moved, but every refusal `change_lane` raises before the spawn (validation, attached task, observed end) happens before the pointer mutation, so a test that injects a pre-launch refusal passes on the unfixed code and the stated control cannot fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both done-whens name test files under `tests/`, a durable repository path, and no scratch or node-local directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags appear in the test filenames, the field names or the prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §17's claim that the pointer moved to `omp-local` attempt 7 with no worker is corroborated by the pointer and the absent attempt-7 stream, and §23's root cause (the fold keyed on the pointer's dialect, with a `claude` fallback in `station_store._fold_stream`) matches the code the plan describes; neither section prescribes a code path or function.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §17 delivers one behaviour (a launch that starts no worker leaves the pointer unmoved and says why) and §23 delivers one rule (each attempt decoded by its own writer's dialect) applied at each reader.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — neither changed section needs a dependency: §23's fixture builds the mixed-harness run without §17's fix, and §17's incident is cited by run id rather than by a declared wait; §23 and §24 are referenced from §17 as its consequences and both resolve.
